solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $u=e^{2x}+1$, so $du=2e^{2x}dx$ and $e^{4x}dx=e^{2x}\cdot e^{2x}dx=\frac12(u-1)\,du$. Then $\int\frac{u-1}{2u^2}du=\frac12\left(\ln u+\frac1u\right)+C$.

**Answer: $\frac12\left(\ln(e^{2x}+1)+\frac1{e^{2x}+1}\right)+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$\sec^4x=\sec^2x(1+\tan^2x)$; with $u=\tan x$: $\int(1+u^2)du=u+\frac{u^3}3+C$.

**Answer: $\tan x+\frac{\tan^3x}3+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The integrand $x^5\sec x$ is an odd function on the symmetric interval $[-5,5]$, so the contributions cancel and the value is $0$. (Since $\sec x$ has simple poles inside $(-5,5)$ at $\pm\frac\pi2,\pm\frac{3\pi}2$, the integral is understood in the principal value sense.)

**Answer: 0**

reviewNote: sec x has non-integrable poles in (-5,5), so the integral only exists as a principal value; the official answer 0 relies on oddness.

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$\frac{\sin3x}{\sin x}=3-4\sin^2x=1+2\cos2x$. So the integral is $\left[x+\sin2x\right]_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}=\pi+(\sin3\pi-\sin\pi)=\pi$.

**Answer: $\pi$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$x^4-x^2-2=(x^2+1)(x^2-2)$, and $\frac{2x^2-1}{(x^2+1)(x^2-2)}=\frac1{x^2+1}+\frac1{x^2-2}$. Then $\int\frac{dx}{x^2-2}=\frac1{2\sqrt2}\ln\left|\frac{x-\sqrt2}{x+\sqrt2}\right|$.

**Answer: $\tan^{-1}x+\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\ln\left|\frac{x-\sqrt2}{x+\sqrt2}\right|+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $u=x^5+1$, $du=5x^4dx$, $x^{10}=(u-1)^2$: the integral is $\frac15\int\frac{(u-1)^2}u du=\frac15\int\left(u-2+\frac1u\right)du=\frac15\left(\frac{u^2}2-2u+\ln|u|\right)+C$. Substituting back, $\frac{(x^5+1)^2}{2}-2(x^5+1)=\frac{x^{10}}2-x^5-\frac32$, and the constant $-\frac32$ can be absorbed into $C$.

**Answer: $\frac15\left(\frac{x^{10}}2-x^5+\ln|x^5+1|\right)+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Cancel $(x-1)^2(x+1)$ from numerator and denominator: the integrand is $\frac1{(x^2+x+1)(x^2+1)}=\frac{x+1}{x^2+x+1}-\frac{x}{x^2+1}$ (partial fractions). Then $\int\frac{x+1}{x^2+x+1}dx=\frac12\ln(x^2+x+1)+\frac1{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt3}$ and $\int\frac x{x^2+1}dx=\frac12\ln(x^2+1)$.

**Answer: $\frac12\ln(x^2+x+1)+\frac1{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt3}-\frac12\ln(x^2+1)+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The radical equals $x^{\frac12+\frac1{2\cdot3}+\frac1{2\cdot3\cdot4}+\cdots}=x^{\frac1{2!}+\frac1{3!}+\cdots}=x^{e-2}$. So the integral is $\int_0^1x^{e-2}dx=\frac1{e-1}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{e-1}$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$\frac1{1+\sec x}=\frac{\cos x}{1+\cos x}=1-\frac1{1+\cos x}=1-\frac12\sec^2\frac x2$. Integrating gives $x-\tan\frac x2+C$, and $\tan\frac x2=\csc x-\cot x$.

**Answer: $x-\csc x+\cot x+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Note $\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{e^{3x}\ln^3x}3\right)=e^{3x}\ln^3x+e^{3x}\frac{\ln^2x}{x}$ (product rule with $\frac{d}{dx}\frac{\ln^3x}{3}=\frac{\ln^2x}x$).

**Answer: $\frac{e^{3x}\ln^3x}{3}+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The integrand is $\frac{x^{1/\varphi}}{(x^\varphi+1)^{1/\varphi}}$. Let $u=x^\varphi+1$; since $\varphi-1=\frac1\varphi$, $du=\varphi x^{\varphi-1}dx=\varphi x^{1/\varphi}dx$. The integral becomes $\frac1\varphi\int_1^2u^{-1/\varphi}du=\frac1\varphi\cdot\frac{2^{1-1/\varphi}-1}{1-1/\varphi}$. With $1-\frac1\varphi=\frac1{\varphi^2}$ this is $\varphi\left(2^{1/\varphi^2}-1\right)$, and $\frac1{\varphi^2}=\frac{3-\sqrt5}2$.

**Answer: $\varphi\left(2^{1/\varphi^2}-1\right)\approx0.4905$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $g(x)=e^{-x^6+x^3+7}$, so $g'(x)=(-6x^5+3x^2)g(x)$ and $-2x^8+x^5=\frac{x^3}3(-6x^5+3x^2)$. Integrating by parts, the integral is $\left[\frac{x^3}3g\right]_{-\infty}^{\infty}-\int x^2g\,dx=-\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}x^2e^{-x^6+x^3+7}dx$. With $u=x^3$: $-\frac13\int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-u^2+u+7}du=-\frac13e^{7+\frac14}\sqrt\pi=-\frac{e^{29/4}\sqrt\pi}3$.

**Answer: $-\frac{e^{29/4}\sqrt\pi}{3}$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
On $[n,n+1)$ the numerator is $n$; $\int_n^\infty\frac{dx}{(x+1)^3}=\frac1{2(n+1)^2}$. So $\int_0^\infty\frac{\lfloor x\rfloor}{(x+1)^3}dx=\sum_{n\ge1}\int_n^\infty\frac{dx}{(x+1)^3}=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1{2(n+1)^2}=\frac12\left(\frac{\pi^2}6-1\right)$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi^2}{12}-\frac12$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
By parts: $\int_0^1x^2\tan^{-1}x\,dx=\left[\frac{x^3}3\tan^{-1}x\right]_0^1-\frac13\int_0^1\frac{x^3}{1+x^2}dx=\frac\pi{12}-\frac13\int_0^1\left(x-\frac x{1+x^2}\right)dx=\frac\pi{12}-\frac13\left(\frac12-\frac12\ln2\right)=\frac16\left(\frac\pi2-1+\ln2\right)$.

**Answer: $\frac16\left(\frac\pi2-1+\ln2\right)$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $u=e^x$, $dx=\frac{du}u$: the integral is $\int_0^\infty\frac{\sin u}u\,du=\frac\pi2$ (the Dirichlet integral).

**Answer: $\frac\pi2$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The inner sum is $\sum_k\frac{(nx^{-n})^k}{k!}=e^{n/x^n}$, so the log of the product is $\sum_{n\ge1}\frac n{x^n}=\frac{1/x}{(1-1/x)^2}=\frac x{(x-1)^2}$. Then $\int_2^3\frac{x}{(x-1)^2}dx=\int_2^3\left(\frac1{x-1}+\frac1{(x-1)^2}\right)dx=\left[\ln(x-1)-\frac1{x-1}\right]_2^3=\left(\ln2-\frac12\right)-(0-1)=\ln2+\frac12$.

**Answer: $\ln2+\frac12$**

reviewNote: Official key says -1/2 - ln 2, a sign error (the integrand x/(x-1)^2 is positive, and numerical integration gives +1.1931); stored ln 2 + 1/2.

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$\frac d{dx}\left(x(\cos x)^x\right)=(\cos x)^x+x(\cos x)^x\left(\ln\cos x-x\tan x\right)=(\cos x)^x(1+x\ln\cos x-x^2\tan x)$, using $\frac d{dx}(\cos x)^x=(\cos x)^x(\ln\cos x-x\tan x)$.

**Answer: $x(\cos x)^x+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$\sin^4x+4\cos^2x=(1-\cos^2x)^2+4\cos^2x=(1+\cos^2x)^2$ and similarly $\cos^4x+4\sin^2x=(1+\sin^2x)^2$. The integrand is $(1+\cos^2x)-(1+\sin^2x)=\cos2x$, so the integral is $\frac12\sin2x+C$.

**Answer: $\frac12\sin2x+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $I$ be the integral and substitute $x\to-x$: since $x\cos x$ is odd, $I=\int\frac{dx}{(1+e^{\cos x})(1+e^{-x\cos x})}$. Averaging the two forms and using $\frac1{1+e^t}+\frac1{1+e^{-t}}=1$ gives $I=\frac12\int_{-\pi}^\pi\frac{dx}{1+e^{\cos x}}=\int_0^\pi\frac{dx}{1+e^{\cos x}}$. Substituting $x\to\pi-x$ gives $\int_0^\pi\frac{dx}{1+e^{-\cos x}}$, and averaging again, $\int_0^\pi\frac{dx}{1+e^{\cos x}}=\frac12\int_0^\pi1\,dx=\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $x=\sin u$: $\int u\sin^2u\cos u\,du=\frac{u\sin^3u}3-\frac13\int\sin^3u\,du=\frac{u\sin^3u}3+\frac{\cos u}3-\frac{\cos^3u}9+C$. Back-substituting: $\frac{x^3\sin^{-1}x}3+\frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}3-\frac{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}9=\frac{x^3\sin^{-1}x}3+\frac{(x^2+2)\sqrt{1-x^2}}9$.

**Answer: $\frac{x^3\sin^{-1}x}{3}+\frac{(x^2+2)\sqrt{1-x^2}}{9}+C$**

reviewNote: Official key gives x^2 sqrt(1-x^2)/9 in the last term, which does not differentiate to x^2 arcsin x; the stored antiderivative was verified by differentiation.

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
First term: with $u=\sin x$, $\int_0^{1/\sqrt2}\sqrt{1-2u^2}\,du=\frac{\pi}{4\sqrt2}$ (a quarter ellipse). Second term: $\int_0^{\pi/4}\sin2x\sqrt{\sin4x}\,dx=\frac12\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin y\sqrt{\sin2y}\,dy$ and by the symmetry $y\to\frac\pi2-y$ this equals $\frac14\int_0^{\pi/2}(\sin y+\cos y)\sqrt{1-(\sin y-\cos y)^2}\,dy$; with $v=\sin y-\cos y$ this is $\frac14\int_{-1}^1\sqrt{1-v^2}dv=\frac\pi8$.

Total: $\frac\pi8+\frac\pi{4\sqrt2}$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi8+\frac{\pi}{4\sqrt2}$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Since $\cot^{-1}x=\frac\pi2-\tan^{-1}x$, we have $(1+\tan^{-1}x)(1+\cot^{-1}x)=1+\frac\pi2+\tan^{-1}x\cot^{-1}x$. Put $a=\tan^{-1}x$, $b=\cot^{-1}x$, $a+b=\frac\pi2$. Then $\frac1{(1+a)(1+b)}=\frac1{2+\pi/2}\left(\frac1{1+a}+\frac1{1+b}\right)$ (because $(1+a)+(1+b)=2+\frac\pi2$). With $\frac{dx}{1+x^2}=da$: $\frac1{2+\pi/2}\int_0^{\pi/4}\left(\frac1{1+a}+\frac1{1+\pi/2-a}\right)da=\frac1{2+\pi/2}\ln(1+\tfrac\pi2)$ The integral of the bracket is $\ln(1+\tfrac\pi4)+\left[\ln(1+\tfrac\pi2)-\ln(1+\tfrac\pi4)\right]=\ln(1+\tfrac\pi2)$, so the value is $\frac{\ln(1+\pi/2)}{2+\pi/2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\ln(1+\pi/2)}{2+\pi/2}$**

prompt: Evaluate $\int_1^\infty\left\lfloor\frac2{\{x\}}\right\rfloor^{-\lfloor x\rfloor}dx$. (Here $\{x\}=x-\lfloor x\rfloor$ is the fractional part.)

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
On $[n,n+1)$ put $u=\{x\}$: the integral is $\sum_{n\ge1}\int_0^1\lfloor2/u\rfloor^{-n}du$. For $u\in\left(\frac2{k+1},\frac2k\right]\cap(0,1]$ we have $\lfloor2/u\rfloor=k$ ($k\ge2$; for $k=2$ this is $(\frac23,1]$). Summing over $n$ first: $\sum_{n\ge1}k^{-n}=\frac1{k-1}$. So the integral is $\sum_{k\ge2}\frac1{k-1}\left(\frac2k-\frac2{k+1}\right)$ over the pieces inside $(0,1)$, which equals $\sum_{k\ge2}\frac{2}{(k-1)k(k+1)}=2\cdot\frac14=\frac12$ (telescoping, $\frac1{(k-1)k(k+1)}=\frac12\left(\frac1{(k-1)k}-\frac1{k(k+1)}\right)$).

**Answer: $\frac12$**

prompt: Evaluate $\int_0^{2025}\min\left(\sqrt{\{x\}-\{x\}^2},\left|\frac{\sqrt3\arcsin(\cos(\pi x))}{\pi}\right|\right)dx$. (Here $\{x\}$ is the fractional part.)

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Both functions have period $1$. The first is $\sqrt{t(1-t)}$, a semicircle of radius $\frac12$ centered at $t=\frac12$. The second, $\frac{\sqrt3}{\pi}\left|\arcsin(\cos\pi x)\right|$, is $\sqrt3\,|t-\tfrac12|$ on $[0,1]$ (a V-shape with slopes $\pm\sqrt3$ with vertex $(\frac12,0)$). Put $s=t-\frac12$. For $|s|<\frac14$ the V is lower; for $\frac14\le|s|\le\frac12$ the semicircle is lower (they meet at $s=\pm\frac14$, at points on the circle $60^\circ$ from the axis). So the area under the minimum over one period is the triangle under the V ($\frac{\sqrt3}{16}$) plus two pieces under the circle, each a $60^\circ$ sector ($\frac\pi{24}$) minus a right triangle ($\frac{\sqrt3}{32}$): total $\frac{\sqrt3}{16}+2\left(\frac\pi{24}-\frac{\sqrt3}{32}\right)=\frac\pi{12}$. Over $2025$ periods the integral is $\frac{2025\pi}{12}$.

**Answer: $\frac{2025\pi}{12}$**
